correctness.rationale: The pathwise Gaussian representation and variance formula are exact. The one-particle hitting lower bound follows from the terminal Gaussian tail, and the upper bound from Borell with a rigorously calculated m(t)<2 sqrt(q). The extreme order-statistic bounds then force T_N/t_N to one uniformly over all nonnegative u_N; uniform weighted t²/t³ expansion gives the complete crossover. The standalone verifier checks nontrivial finite cases but is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The singular absence of thermal positional noise changes extreme search from ordinary Brownian logarithmic kinetics to kinetic acceleration-limited powers. A quantifiable critical shrinking initial-velocity variance drives a transition of extreme search exponents, and the theorem produces a whole continuous interpolation and finite-N Gaussian crossing bounds. These resolve an identifiable natural physical regime rather than a routine variable renaming.
